races.name: On The River Ball+Chain Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Absolute Diamond
runners_data.note: Best recent form in the field (second on soft, placed on similar going), trained by David Evans who fires regularly with juveniles; the only runner with any front-running inclination and Ryan Kavanagh's booking adds a 3lb claim — if this one leads, it is doing so into a vacuum rather than against opposition.
runners_data.comment: Our top-rated of the seven and nine pounds above her official mark, Absolute Diamond rates the one to beat on figures, with today distance and going already met and a recent outing 16 days back. Yet to win in her last three and only sixth last time out the reservation, but the numbers keep her on top.

runners_data.name: Il Capo
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon yard is 7/56 over 14 days (solid strike rate), Joe Leavy takes the ride on a horse whose three runs have all been on going similar to today; true hold-up style means it needs traffic to part naturally in a bunched sprint finish — the 6f trip looks adequate but a step back to 6f from 7f is noted.
runners_data.comment: A repeated finisher down the field, having come home eighth, seventh and sixth in his last three starts without a win. He does have experience of today's distance and going and returns after 18 days, but sixth of seven on our figures he has plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Dreams Galore
runners_data.note: Charles Bishop partners this Ollie Sangster runner who has shown a tendency to finish off races without threatening the winner; hold-up in style, drops to a career-low trip of 6f (both previous 6f runs modest), and the stable's 5/22 T14 rate suggests some form — though the 5f runs suggest this trip is already testing its stamina range.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger on our figures, ranked third of seven after finishing seventh, fourth and seventh in her last three starts. She has run over today's trip before and returns 18 days on from that effort, though the mixed sequence of finishes is the obvious risk.

runners_data.name: Sovereign Beach
runners_data.note: Ollie Sangster double-handed here with a horse whose last three runs include a fifth and sixth on good and soft; its true running style is held-up from off the pace, though with the field stacked with closers it is likely to race closer to the pace than it wants — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.90) tempers enthusiasm even if the form line is not disgraced.
runners_data.comment: A midfield contender on our figures, fifth of seven having been unplaced, sixth and fifth in her last three starts without a win. She has run over today's distance and going before, but a 31-day break since that latest run leaves her fitness up for debate.

runners_data.name: Havananother
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes sends this one out with a 7lb apprentice (Donagh Murphy) on a horse that has finished fifth and seventh in its last two — genuinely held-up by nature but squeezed into a midfield slot by the map because the rear is overcrowded; the stable's 3/26 T14 rate is modest and the form string (578) does not demand respect at present.
runners_data.comment: Rated a leading danger, fourth of seven having finished eighth, seventh and fifth in her last three starts. She has run over today's distance and going before and is quick to return on a 16-day turnaround, though yet to break into the placings this term.

runners_data.name: So Tempting
runners_data.note: Tom Ward has had no winners in 14 days (0/9) and this runner's form figures of 866 are the weakest in the field; held-up in style but mapped to midfield due to congestion at the rear, wears a hood (hg:p), and ran on good ground in its last two starts without threatening — the headgear is worth noting as a first-time angle but the evidence of ability is thin.
runners_data.comment: A notable danger on our figures, second of seven despite a modest run of sixth, sixth and eighth in her last three starts. She has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly on a 15-day turnaround, though the finishing form has yet to match her promise.

runners_data.name: Devon Angel
runners_data.note: Rod Millman's runner is the lowest-rated in the field at OR 45 but returned a third last time out on good ground over 5f, suggesting it has ability at sprint distances; Tyler Heard rides, and the step up to 6f from 5f is an unknown — held-up by style but redistributed to midfield, its most likely role is as a place contender if the sprint finish develops wide and clean.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of the weights and last of seven on our figures, she has managed only third, sixth, unplaced and seventh in her last four starts without a win. She has run over today's trip before and returns after 10 days, with her trainer in good current form.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field, this 6f nursery at Chepstow on good-to-firm ground is likely to be run at a steady, dawdling gallop before the field bunches and explodes into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole. Absolute Diamond is the only runner with a style code suggesting any inclination to race prominently, and even that is uncertain, meaning the pace is likely to be modest and the race will be decided by finishing speed rather than stamina. The overwhelming majority of the field — Il Capo, Dreams Galore, Sovereign Beach, Havananother, So Tempting, and Devon Angel — are all hold-up types by nature, and four of them (Sovereign Beach, Havananother, So Tempting, Devon Angel) have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply too many closers for them all to race from the rear; the runners most likely to actually secure a genuine rearward position are Il Capo and Dreams Galore, with the redistributed quartet likely to find themselves racing closer than ideal. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape strongly favours a horse with a sharp, late turn of foot who can produce a powerful finishing burst in the final furlong — the closers and midfield-to-late runners hold the structural advantage, but only those with genuine finishing speed on good-to-firm ground will capitalise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Sprint Finish, Closers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is as slow as the lack of front-runners suggests and the race becomes a six-furlong sprint from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: The field crawls through the early stages, compresses into a tight bunch turning for home, and the final furlong becomes a flat-out dash where finishing acceleration is everything; horses with a sharp, late kick on fast ground gain a decisive edge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Absolute Diamond Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Absolute Diamond breaks well and Kavanagh elects to take advantage of the leadership vacuum, setting a controlled but not soft pace.
scenarios.body: Racing from the front on good-to-firm ground over 6f, Absolute Diamond could control the tempo and, if the pace is fair rather than crawling, deny the hold-up horses a target to run at; a horse that finds relaxation and travels sweetly in front can often hold on in a small field when rivals cannot coordinate their challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Grinders Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution holds and several supposed closers race in a pack mid-division, with the race developing into a sustained grind rather than a pure sprint.
scenarios.body: With multiple hold-up horses bumping into one another mid-race and unable to find clear daylight until late, a horse that threads through and sustains its run longest benefits; Devon Angel's recent third on good ground and Sovereign Beach's course form give them a place angle here.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos, Long-Shot Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the slow pace causes crowding, a false start effect, or a runner gets a completely uncontested split through the pack.
scenarios.body: In a bunched, tactical 6f sprint with seven two-year-olds and no traffic management, a lower-rated runner can find a golden passage and beat the field for a stride or two that proves decisive; the wide-margin nursery format and young, inexperienced fields make this scenario live even if unlikely.

watchPoints.text: Watch Absolute Diamond's early stride — if Ryan Kavanagh pushes forward from the gate and secures the lead uncontested, the entire race shape pivots from a sprint finish to a controlled front-running scenario that fundamentally changes which horses can win.

Monitor how the four redistributed hold-up types (Sovereign Beach, Havananother, So Tempting, Devon Angel) break from the gates — if they all miss the start and end up genuinely at the rear, the track becomes one-dimensional and a sprint-finish bunching scenario becomes near-certain.

So Tempting wears a hood for the first time (hg:p) for Tom Ward — headgear debutants in juveniles can produce unpredictable early behaviour, including unexpected forward movement, which could accidentally inject pace into what is otherwise expected to be a dawdling race.

Devon Angel is the freshest in the field at only 10 days since last run and showed a place effort on good ground — short-turnaround runners for Millman in nurseries can arrive fit and ready, and the drop in class relative to OR 45 makes it a legitimate watch for each-way purposes.

The going report confirms good-to-firm conditions throughout the card at Chepstow today — faster ground will emphasise finishing speed over stamina, reinforcing the sprint-finish shape and benefiting horses with a sharp, late kick rather than those who need a genuine test to see out the 6f.

races.name: Apex Transport Planning Summer Sunset / EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Cheeseburger Aaron Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Brave Byreflection
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse whose recent handicap form shows finishes deep in the field at this trip and trip-up on Standard going; James Evans sends her out 25 days fresh and the similar-going record (1W from 15) gives little confidence, though Good to Firm is at least not a concern.
runners_data.comment: Sits highest of these seven on our figures, with the fastest speed figure in the race hinting at more ability than recent finishes suggest. Winless in her last five starts, she has run over today's distance and going before, and that below-par record is the query, but the figures make her the one to beat.

runners_data.name: On Key
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with strong 7f and 6f placed form on Good; Kieran O'Neill rides and a ten-day turnaround suggests Scott Dixon is confident, with one win and a placed finish in 15 similar-going starts underpinning solid each-way claims.
runners_data.comment: Held on our figures at sixth of seven despite a fair recent record, having won once and been placed four times in his last six starts. He has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly after 10 days, but the rating gap to the principals here is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Francisco
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse whose natural rear-running style is crowded out here, forcing him wider in the field than ideal — his 7f record is strong (1W, 2P in 15 similar-going runs) and a visor is worn, but the 50-day absence and the positional compromise are both negatives.
runners_data.comment: A fair case exists for this midfield runner, a winner three starts back and rarely far away since, with efforts of eighth, sixth, first, third and fourth in his last five starts. He has run over today's distance and going before, though a 50-day absence since that run raises a fitness question.

runners_data.name: Too Much Trevor
runners_data.note: Ashley Lewis (5lb claim) takes the ride on this prominent performer with a very strong recent record — nine placings from 15 similar-going starts including wins over 7f and 6f on Good — and an eight-day turnaround signals peak fitness; well placed to capitalise if Auburn Avenue's pace is catchable.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our figures despite winning last time out, a form line backed up by placed efforts either side of that latest success in his last six starts. He has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly after eight days, but ranked last of seven he has plenty to find on official figures.

runners_data.name: Sioux Warrior
runners_data.note: Genuine closer whose best form comes from off the pace over 7f and 6f on Good — the headgear (p) is retained — but with the hold-up berths oversubscribed he is pushed into midfield against his instincts; the style-fit discount (0.91) tempers his chance, even though his recent record shows a win and four places from 15 similar-going outings.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger, a winner last time out following a string of frame finishes beforehand. He has run over today's distance and going before and returns after 16 days, but fourth of seven on our figures there is a little more to find against the principals.

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: In the form of her life with three wins in five runs on Good ground over 7f and 8f, including a course win; hold-up style under Mason Paetel (5lb claim) is natural and her historical similar-going figures (3W, 5P) are the strongest in the field — her main risk is whether the pace falls in her favour.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger, having won her last two starts and three of her last six, with placed efforts either side of those wins. She has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly on a seven-day turnaround, but sits only third of seven on our figures with a little more to find.

runners_data.name: Auburn Avenue
runners_data.note: Charles Bishop partners this confirmed front-runner, who steps back from 8f to 7f and faces a tricky trainer spell (John & Thys Flint 0/7 in 14 days); the style-fit tag (0.93) reflects that solo front-running at a sustainable clip may prove a double-edged sword if prominent rivals sit close enough to challenge.
runners_data.comment: A significant danger on our figures, second of seven despite a mixed run of seventh, eighth, second, seventh and fourth without a win in that sequence. She has run over today's trip before and returns after a 17-day break, though the inconsistency behind that runner-up effort is the obvious risk.

races.paceDynamic: Auburn Avenue is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just one confirmed pace-setter in a seven-runner field, she is set to control this 7f contest at Chepstow on Good to Firm ground without meaningful pressure from a rival leader. Too Much Trevor and On Key will press from prominent positions and keep Auburn Avenue honest, but neither is a natural front-runner, meaning the pace is likely to be sustainable rather than burning — the shape that classically rewards hold-up runners who can pick up in the straight. This field holds more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear; Francisco and Sioux Warrior are genuine closers who will be shuffled into midfield against their natural instincts, with On Key and Too Much Trevor most likely to actually secure the prominent positions behind Auburn Avenue. The race shape therefore favours a prominent-to-midfield profile that can travel comfortably in a steadily-run contest and still find a gear in the final two furlongs — pure closers are compromised by the redistribution at the rear.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Auburn Avenue dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the field strings out in a single-file pursuit through the first half.
scenarios.body: Auburn Avenue sets fractions that suit herself and the nearest prominent stalkers, and with no rival applying early heat the tempo never fully stretches the field out; runners with the gate speed to sit just behind the leader travel on the bridle and have enough stamina to sprint clear late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fractionally quicker than expected and the prominent runners are left flat-footed in the straight.
scenarios.body: The front and prominent group empty inside the final furlong, opening a window for runners held off the pace to weave through beaten rivals; however, Francisco and Sioux Warrior are racing out of their natural hold-up roles, reducing the chance this shape produces its expected winner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Clears Up
scenarios.trigger: If Auburn Avenue steals first run turning for home and the moderate gallop catches her rivals flat-footed.
scenarios.body: A slow-burning pace means no one applies pressure early enough to unsettle Auburn Avenue, and she stretches clear before hold-up horses can get organised; Too Much Trevor or On Key may chase without ever fully closing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If early jostling for position causes interference and the field bunches, scrambling the expected race shape entirely.
scenarios.body: Compressed early order disrupts the preferred tracking positions of On Key and Too Much Trevor, gifting an advantage to whoever emerges cleanest from the melee; in this scenario fresh, handily-drawn horses with strong recent form can outrun their odds.

watchPoints.text: Prefer The Sister has three wins from five starts on Good ground at 7f, and if the pace is sufficient to stretch the field, Mason Paetel could time a run through to devastating effect — the most dangerous closer in the race.

Too Much Trevor's eight-day turnaround and strong similar-going record (9 placings from 15) make her a serious threat to lead or track Auburn Avenue; if she gets first run from a prominent position the hold-up horses may not have time to reel her in.

Francisco and Sioux Warrior are both genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield roles by overcrowding at the rear — watch for both being shuffled wide or short of room when the field accelerates, compromising their chance regardless of ability.

Auburn Avenue's trainer John & Thys Flint have returned 0/7 in the last 14 days — if the horse is below peak condition, the controlled front-running role could unravel quickly once Too Much Trevor or On Key applies pressure at the two-furlong pole.

races.name: LSL Racing Horse Sales Handicap Stakes (Chepstow Mile Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Dapper Gee Gee
runners_data.note: Prominent racer whose best form comes when able to press the pace, and Tony Carroll's yard is in solid form (5/31 over 14 days); the step back up to a mile on Good to Firm is the slight query given his recent form at 7f on soft, with similar-going record of just 3 placed from 15.
runners_data.comment: A balanced case for this midfield runner, a winner three starts back with a strong speed figure, but form has since cooled with a second and a fifth in the two runs since. He has run over today's distance and going before, though a 42-day absence leaves his fitness open to question.

runners_data.name: Eutropia
runners_data.note: Back quickly after a run just eight days ago but Adrian Wintle's 2/12 T14 strike-rate is fair, and this mare has placed twice in her last two on Good ground at a mile — the trip and surface are clearly in her favour and she looks the most in-form of the prominent types.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated of this seven and the one to beat, runner-up in each of her last two starts after back-to-back wins four and five starts back. She has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly on an eight-day turnaround, with only a below-par fifth earlier in that sequence to give pause.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of The Bay
runners_data.note: An eight-year-old hold-up horse who carries a hood and has a solid recent record at this trip on Good ground (2nd, 4th, 4th in last three at 8f/Good); John & Rhys Flint have had no runners in the past 14 days which is worth noting, but Spirit Of The Bay's class ceiling on OR 64 is the limiting factor.
runners_data.comment: A significant danger on our figures, second of seven with the second-fastest speed figure in the race, having been runner-up last time out. She has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly after 10 days, though a string of modest efforts before that placed run is the query.

runners_data.name: Rating
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up performer by nature but the race shape pushes this horse into a midfield role rather than the rear; the form string shows a win at 8f/Firm and consistent placing on Good, though the apprentice Lewis (5) claim helps offset the weight and the style mismatch is the key discount.
runners_data.comment: Held on our figures at sixth of seven, though not without claims, having won four starts back and remained competitive since with a third and two fifths. She has run over today's distance and going before and returns quickly after eight days, but the gap to the principals here looks the difference.

runners_data.name: Nammos
runners_data.note: Another true hold-up horse by inclination whose natural finishing kick is blunted by an effective midfield position in this race shape — Nammos has won twice on Firm and placed on Good at this trip, but an OR of just 55 and no placed run in the last six make this a tough ask even if the style mismatch were not a factor.
runners_data.comment: Bottom of our seven on figures, but a win and a pair of seconds in her last six show the ability is there. She has run over today distance and going before and returns after 16 days, though two subsequent fifths leave her hard to fancy on our numbers.

runners_data.name: Kodi Fire
runners_data.note: Charles Hills sends this four-year-old back to Chepstow's mile where he won last time out on Good, and the tongue-tie/hood headgear combination is clearly working; with a STYLE_FIT flag of 0.93 as a prominent type who found himself leading last time, his ability to dictate at a sustainable gallop is both his biggest strength and the scenario the entire race hinges around.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger, a winner last time out and owner of the fastest speed figure in the race. He has run over today's distance and going before and is quick to return on an eight-day turnaround, but a modest sequence before that victory leaves him third of seven on our figures.

runners_data.name: Darvel
runners_data.note: Patrick Chamings's eight-year-old is the classiest closer in the race on the evidence of his OR 69 and strong recent Good-ground record at this trip (2nd, 3rd in last two); blinkers fitted, Charles Bishop booked — the danger is simply whether Kodi Fire's tempo is strong enough to bring him into it from the rear.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger back in good heart, third last time out and runner-up the start before, both since a spell of two unplaced efforts. He has today distance and going experience and runs off 15 days, winless in his last six but clearly back on track.

races.paceDynamic: Kodi Fire is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in a field of just seven, Harry Vigors can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the outset on Good to Firm ground at Chepstow's straight mile. Dapper Gee Gee and Eutropia are both prominent types who will seek to track closely, meaning the early order should settle quickly with Kodi Fire in front and those two sitting just off the pace. The field contains more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear — Rating and Nammos, though natural hold-up horses, are effectively mapped to midfield positions they would not freely choose, and Darvel and Spirit Of The Bay are the true closers sitting furthest back. A single, uncontested front-runner setting a measured pace on fast ground is a textbook scenario for the leader to control the tempo and have something left in the final furlong, making prominent racers — particularly those positioned just behind Kodi Fire — the most favoured profile in this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kodi Fire Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kodi Fire leads uncontested at a measured gallop and the field fails to close the gap entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Kodi Fire dictates every yard from the front, with Vigors able to manage the pace on Good to Firm ground, and the solo leader has enough in reserve to repel challengers; prominent horses Dapper Gee Gee and Eutropia, sitting just off the pace, are best placed to capitalise if Kodi Fire ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Kodi Fire's pace proves just quick enough to set the race up for the prominent horses stalking immediately behind.
scenarios.body: Dapper Gee Gee or Eutropia, racing with cover in second and third, produce their finishing effort before the final furlong and wear down a tiring Kodi Fire; both have shown the ability to win off this sort of OR on comparable going and Chepstow's straight mile suits horses who travel well through a race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Reel Them In Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kodi Fire sets a stronger-than-expected pace that strings the field out and leaves the leaders vulnerable to late challengers.
scenarios.body: Darvel, with the best recent form credentials in the field and proven ability to finish strongly on Good ground, would be the primary beneficiary as would Spirit Of The Bay if able to produce a decisive late run; however Rating and Nammos, though natural hold-up types, are not truly at the rear and their closing kicks are diluted by their forced midfield positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Deliver
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run at a genuinely fast clip that suits pure closers and the redistributed midfield types manage to find a passage late.
scenarios.body: This scenario depends heavily on Rating and Nammos racing out of their true role and finding the kind of closing run they would naturally produce from further back, which the current race shape actively works against; Darvel remains the most plausible beneficiary even here, given his genuine hold-up credentials and class-leading OR.

watchPoints.text: Kodi Fire's early pace — if Vigors elects to go slow from the front, the race could turn into a sprint from two furlongs out, flattening the form book entirely and making the finish unpredictable.
Darvel's closing run from the rear — Bishop will need a clear passage on the rail or wide into the straight; traffic at Chepstow's mile can be a genuine obstacle for late-closers in small fields.
Eutropia's rapid return after just eight days — she ran two days short of a week ago and, while her recent form is strong, any residual fatigue could blunt her finishing effort in the straight.

Rating and Nammos are both forced into midfield positions that do not reflect their true running style; if either drifts back toward their natural hold-up position during the race, their effective STYLE_FIT discount is compounded further.

Dapper Gee Gee's form at a mile is unproven on quick ground — five of his last six runs have been on soft or standard, and a step up to Good to Firm at this trip is a genuine unknown worth monitoring in running.

races.name: 3A's Caravan & Motorhome Classified Stakes

runners_data.name: Judge Frank
runners_data.note: Trainer John & Rhys Flint have gone 0/7 in the last 14 days and Charles Bishop takes the ride on a horse whose form figures of 7-7-8-8 give little confidence; a true hold-up performer that the map shifts forward to midfield given the excess of rear-runners, and similar-going form (7/15) offers no encouragement.
runners_data.comment: A modest recent record for this midfield runner, with finishes no better than seventh across his last five starts including two eighths. He has run over today's distance and going before, but a 39-day break since that last effort and the lack of a placed run leave plenty to prove.

runners_data.name: Knightmare
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pace-maker, David Evans sends him here on 17 days' rest with a consistent placed record (5 seconds in recent starts) and he qualifies as a front-runner mapped to prominent because he is the one horse likely to actually seize the lead uncontested; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim could help him conserve energy.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger, remarkably consistent with four runner-up efforts among his last six starts, missing only a modest fifth in between. He has run over today's trip before and returns after 17 days, still without a win in that sequence, but the placed record makes him hard to leave out.

runners_data.name: Lady Margret
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll runner returning from a lengthy 186-day absence, and a horse that has not shown similar-going form — just 1 placing from 6 starts on comparable ground — making the layoff and going combination twin concerns; Jack Doughty takes the ride.
runners_data.comment: An outsider on our figures, eighth of ten after a modest recent sequence including two unplaced efforts among her last five starts without a win. She has run over today's trip before, but a lengthy 186-day absence since her last outing is the major concern here.

runners_data.name: Prince Ali
runners_data.note: Won last time out on soft at 8f with the headgear (p) clearly helping and Thomas Faulkner's yard is 1/3 in the last fortnight, giving this eight-year-old rare live credentials; Zoe Lewis's 7lb claim is significant and his ability to travel prominently off a slow pace suits this shape well.
runners_data.comment: Top-rated of this ten having won last time out, a form line that stands out among an otherwise modest sequence of sixth, third, seventh, eighth and seventh. He has run over today's distance and going before, but a 48-day gap since that win and the patchy form before it are the risks.

runners_data.name: Star Of Atlantis
runners_data.note: Wears headgear (h) and Adrian Wintle's yard is 2/12 in the past two weeks, but a form string of 9-8-5-8-4-6 tells its own story; naturally a rear-runner whose position on the map reflects the crowded hold-up division rather than a genuine style shift, and Joe Leavy's task is to coax more than this record suggests.
runners_data.comment: Our selection, rated three pounds above her current official mark and open to more than her finishing positions of sixth, fourth, eighth, fifth, eighth and ninth suggest. She has run over today's trip before and returns on a fresh 23-day turnaround, with the lack of a placed run in that sequence the clear reservation.

runners_data.name: Strong Man Tom
runners_data.note: Barry John Murphy's lightly-raced four-year-old wears a tongue-tie and has managed only three runs, all in soft or good ground at longer trips than today's mile; flagged as likely to fade in the finish and genuinely one of the hold-up runners pushed into midfield on the map by weight of numbers — the step up in class and speed of ground are both concerns.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced and open to improvement, with unplaced, sixth and sixth in his last three starts showing modest but workable form without a win. He returns after a 46-day break, and with more experience to come there is room for this profile to strengthen.

runners_data.name: Weston Court
runners_data.note: A horse that ran just eight days ago and returns quickly for R Harris, who is 0/2 in the fortnight; the visor is retained and a form line of 4-4-2-5-6 on good-to-firm and good shows genuine competitiveness, making him one of the more interesting hold-up types remapped to midfield — his sharp recent activity could leave him short.
runners_data.comment: Well down our figures at ninth of ten, with a runner-up effort three starts back the highlight of an otherwise middling sequence. He has run over today's distance and going before and is quick to return after eight days, but there is a lot of ground to find here.

runners_data.name: A Rose Adaay
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's four-year-old has placed twice in her last five runs and is consistent enough to be competitive; normally settles in rear but the abundance of hold-up horses means she will likely race further forward than customary — Ben Ffrench Davis's 5lb claim is a help and she has strong claims on similar going (4 starts, 1 placing).
runners_data.comment: A fair case for this midfield runner, fourth of ten and rarely too far away with two thirds among her last five starts without a win. She has run over today's distance and going before, though a 24-day gap since her last outing leaves a slight fitness question over today's run.

runners_data.name: Fighting Queen
runners_data.note: John & Rhys Flint's runner carries the same trainer's 0/7 recent form and William Carson rides a mare whose last two outings produced zeros; similar-going evidence is thin at 5 starts and 0 wins or places, and returning from 41 days off adds another layer of uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: A leading danger on our figures, second of ten, with a third her best effort among five modest runs. She has run over today's distance and going before, though winless in that sequence and a 41-day absence since raise obvious questions.

runners_data.name: Fitzmaurice
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's second runner here wears a hood and George Wood partners; a horse who has finished no better than fifth in six recent starts, all on standard or good ground at 6f-8f, and naturally a rear-runner whose midfield map position reflects the field's overcrowded hold-up section rather than any genuine tactical flexibility.
runners_data.comment: Well down our figures at seventh of ten, Fitzmaurice has finished no better than fifth in his last six and was only eighth last time out. He has today distance and going experience and returns after 11 days, but on these efforts he is hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Knightmare is the sole confirmed front-runner in this ten-runner field and, with no rival likely to seriously contest the lead, David Evans's four-year-old should coast to the front early and set a comfortable, sustainable gallop over the mile trip on going that is riding Good to Firm throughout the card. That uncontested lead on a flat track with a genuine pace-setter dictating matters strongly favours a horse who can travel prominently and challenge from a position of comfort rather than one grinding from deep. The field is overwhelmingly composed of hold-up types, and with just one pace-maker the tempo may be controlled and even-paced rather than searching, limiting the runway available for closers to build momentum from the rear. This shape strongly favours a horse that can sit close to Knightmare in second or third and deliver a sustained challenge in the final two furlongs rather than a true deep hold-up runner. Several horses listed — including A Rose Adaay, Star Of Atlantis, Judge Frank, Weston Court, Fitzmaurice, and Strong Man Tom — are genuine hold-up types who have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field contains far more rear-runners than the race shape can accommodate; of these, A Rose Adaay and Weston Court, with their better recent form figures, are best placed to actually work into contention from a more forward pitch than usual.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Knightmare Dictates Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Knightmare crosses cleanly, settles on a comfortable lead and is not pressured into stretching the field at any stage.
scenarios.body: Knightmare sets a controlled, even pace that suits a close-up chaser and the lack of genuine front-running rivals means the tempo is entirely in Evans's hands; the race becomes a test of who can pick up most efficiently from a steady gallop in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Chaser Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest enough that a horse travelling in second or third can wear down Knightmare without needing a sustained sprint.
scenarios.body: Prince Ali, who won last time on soft, can travel sweetly just off the pace and his visor may sharpen his focus on this faster ground; A Rose Adaay has the consistency to deliver a strong late challenge from just off the lead if she gets a better position than usual.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to string the field out and leave genuine closers with a meaningful gap to exploit in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A fast-ground surface and a solo front-runner rarely create the scorching pace required for true closers, but Weston Court's recent 4-4-2 form on similar ground gives her the best credentials among the hold-up contingent if conditions conspire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Messy Pace, Bunch Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the controlled tempo collapses into a crawl and the whole field bunches turning for home, producing a sprint finish that scrambles the form.
scenarios.body: In a compressed finish headgear could matter — Fitzmaurice wears a hood and Weston Court a visor — but neither has shown the finishing speed to take full advantage, and Strong Man Tom's tendency to fade makes this scenario his least likely vehicle for success.

watchPoints.text: Knightmare — if he crosses quickly from stall position and gets uncontested, his controlled front-running over a flat mile on fast ground makes him the most dangerous single horse in this race shape.

Prince Ali — watch the market move for this course-inexperienced but recent winner; if he travels close to Knightmare under Zoe Lewis's 7lb claim, the combination of positional advantage and claiming allowance could make him a live threat.

Lady Margret — returning from 186 days off is a significant flag; watch the parade ring for any sign of sweat or edginess that might compound the layoff concern before committing any opinion on her chance.

A Rose Adaay and Weston Court — both are natural hold-up horses who may attempt to race more prominently than usual given the single pace-maker; if either secures a forward berth early, reassess their chances upward versus the listed odds.

Strong Man Tom — the fade warning combined with a tongue-tie debut at this trip and on faster ground than he has encountered suggests he may be a reliable guide to the pace in the first half of the race rather than a genuine contender in the closing stages.

races.name: Sophie Busson Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Trafalger
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer with two placed efforts on Good going in its recent history (3rd 2/5f/GOO, 2/5f/GOO); Benoit de la Sayette takes over and Ben Case's yard is quiet at 0/5 in 14 days, so needs the race to truly develop late to make its finishing effort count.
runners_data.comment: Trafalger arrives without a win in his last five starts but was second as far back as five starts ago, dipping to only eighth last time out. He has run over today's trip and going before, benefits from a 25-day breather, and tops our figures — though that below-par latest run is the risk.

runners_data.name: Savannah Smiles
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good 8 days ago and has a strong recent record of placing (10/15 on similar going), making it the most in-form hold-up runner in the field; hg:p (hood) may aid concentration, and Harry Vigors' 5lb claim is a meaningful weight advantage at 135lbs claimed down.
runners_data.comment: Savannah Smiles has won once in her last six starts and added three further placings, including when second last time out. Proven over this trip and going and back quickly after just eight days, she rates a leading danger, though our figures marginally prefer others.

runners_data.name: Level Up
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with five placed finishes from five runs on similar going, though its true style is hold-up and it is pushed forward on the map only because the rear is saturated — the 0.92 style-fit flag tempers expectations; Ashley Lewis's 5lb claim softens the weight, and the blinkered headgear may encourage a sharper early response.
runners_data.comment: Level Up has finished second in each of his last three starts, a progressive profile that makes him our pick here. He has run over today's trip and going before and is out again quickly on just four days, with turning those places into a win the obvious next step.

runners_data.name: So Smart
runners_data.note: Mapped to the lead as the only horse likely to set the pace; its true style is prominent rather than front-running and the 0.80 style-fit tag means it is racing out of role, but there is simply no confirmed rival to take the job — won over 5f on Good recently and handles this going, making it the key pace-setter by default; Grace Harris has 3/15 in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: So Smart won last time out and has been frequently competitive before that, placed third in three of his last six starts. He has run over today's trip and going before, returns quickly after eight days, and carries a strong speed figure of 75 that marks him as one of the leading dangers.

runners_data.name: Son Of Astar
runners_data.note: A troubled recent form string (5/0/6/0/2/0) with significant non-completion flags and erratic finishing positions makes it an unreliable commodity; Tony Carroll's yard is active (5/31) but a 41-day absence and a style-fit discount from redistribution mean this horse needs everything to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Son Of Astar remains without a win in his last six starts, though he was runner-up two starts back and has flashes of ability among mostly modest form. He has run over today's trip and going before, but returns following a lengthy 41-day absence that leaves questions over readiness.

runners_data.name: Sundiata Keita
runners_data.note: Dropping sharply to 5f from a background over 6-7f, and all five recent runs have been over 6f or longer — the trip looks short; its true style is hold-up and the redistribution to midfield means it is squeezed into a position it cannot exploit, with the John & Rhys Flint yard having no returns in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Sundiata Keita is without a win in his last five starts and has been well beaten more often than not, including a ninth two starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fairly fresh on 16 days, but his low rating leaves plenty to find with this field.

runners_data.name: River Edge
runners_data.note: All five recent runs have been on Good ground, showing admirable consistency in going terms, with three placed efforts; Christopher Mason's yard has one winner from six in the past fortnight, and the 116lb weight gives a significant pull — its natural hold-up style is displaced by redistribution but strong course-specific going form makes it one to monitor if traffic clears.
runners_data.comment: River Edge remains without a win in his last five starts, though he was runner-up three starts back and has rarely finished far off the pace. He has run over today's trip and going before, returns quickly on just eight days, and shows a useful speed figure of 72 despite ranking last of the seven on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: So Smart is the only confirmed pace-setter in this 7-runner 5f handicap at Chepstow, though the REDISTRIBUTED flags reveal that Level Up, Son Of Astar, Sundiata Keita and River Edge are all genuine hold-up horses pushed into midfield positions on the map because the rear is oversubscribed — none of them are naturally at home racing prominently. So Smart will roll forward from the gates on Good to Firm ground and, with no genuine rival to pressure it, is likely to control tempo from the front in a measured rather than breakneck fashion, producing a race that runs at a steady-to-fair gallop rather than a true test. Trafalger and Savannah Smiles are the authentic hold-up operators here, with the latter showing strong recent form across similar going and a win just 8 days ago, making them the runners best equipped to finish through. This race shape — a single soft-galloped leader, an overcrowded hold-up division, and a proper Good to Firm surface — most favours closers with a genuine turn of foot in the final furlong, provided the pace is sufficient to set them up; on a flat 5f course with this tempo profile, horses that can produce a sustained late run rather than a sharp sprint are at an advantage. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can naturally accommodate, with So Smart and potentially Savannah Smiles the most likely to actually secure their preferred positions at the front end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: So Smart Dictates Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If So Smart breaks cleanly and controls a steady tempo unchallenged from flag to finish.
scenarios.body: So Smart sets a comfortable gallop on Good to Firm ground and, with no genuine rival matching it for pace early, builds a winning lead into the final furlong that the crowded hold-up group cannot overhaul in time. This shape rewards the horse racing in its natural role at the front and punishes the redistributed hold-up types who cannot produce the required finishing burst off a slow pace.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves sufficient and the genuine hold-up horses find clear running through the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Trafalger and Savannah Smiles, as the authentic hold-up operators in this field, are best placed to finish powerfully if So Smart's early tempo is fast enough to create a meaningful contest in the closing stages. Savannah Smiles brings excellent recent form — a win 8 days ago over similar ground — and at a competitive weight could run down a tiring leader in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Chaos, Eyecatcher Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If early traffic problems disrupt the hold-up runners and one of the redistributed midfield types finds room late.
scenarios.body: Level Up has the profile of a genuine hold-up horse forced wide on the map, and its consistent placed form over 5f on similar going gives it a chance if it can manoeuvre through the crowded midfield in the closing stages. River Edge brings all five recent runs on Good ground with placed efforts and could capitalise if the inner rail opens up at the critical moment.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Fight It Out
scenarios.trigger: If a rival challenges So Smart early and the race develops into a pace duel that suits nothing finishing from behind.
scenarios.body: A contested lead would burn off So Smart's advantage and leave the hold-up division with even less time to close, producing a flat-out sprint between the front runners that neither true closer can reach. This scenario is unlikely given the absence of any confirmed front runner to apply pressure, but Son Of Astar's inconsistent form makes it a wildcard if breaking sharply.

watchPoints.text: So Smart is the only genuine pace-setter and must break cleanly — if it misses the kick, no confirmed leader replaces it and the entire race shape collapses into a muddled sprint with no obvious beneficiary.

The rear of this field is severely overcrowded with genuine hold-up types (Level Up, Son Of Astar, Sundiata Keita, River Edge all redistributed), meaning significant traffic is likely in the final two furlongs — watch for blocked runs on the rail.

Savannah Smiles runs just 8 days after its last start with headgear applied; if the hood has an exaggerated effect on early behaviour it could compromise the hold-up position that is central to its chance.

River Edge's five-from-five record on Good ground is the strongest going-specific fit in the field and merits watching in running if it finds a clear passage from its midfield slot despite the style-fit displacement.
Son Of Astar has a 41-day absence and a string of zeros in recent form — watch its behaviour in the stalls and early strides as a guide to whether it is fit enough to factor at all.

races.name: Weir Mechanical Solutions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Crimson Road
runners_data.note: Ran well at 10f on Good in her last start and her sim-going record of 12 runs on similar ground (one win, one place) underlines she handles conditions; natural hold-up horse who will need William Carson to push her closer to the pace than usual to exploit this race's lone front-runner scenario.
runners_data.comment: Crimson Road is without a win in his last five starts, fourth last time out, and a fifth three starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, returns following a 22-day break, and a leading speed figure of 73 sees him head our figures over this longer trip.

runners_data.name: Brodie's Boy
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's consistent yard sent out five winners in 14 days and this horse has placed at 11-12f on comparable going, but a sim-going record of just three runs and zero wins raises a flag; drops to the midfield in this map as a hold-up type, and a clean run through a crowded late pack will be essential for George Wood.
runners_data.comment: Brodie's Boy has been frequently in the frame this term, fourth two starts back and third five starts back, though he remains without a win in his last six outings. He has run over today's trip and going before and is fit from a run just 16 days ago — our selection on the strength of that rounded profile rather than outright figures.

runners_data.name: Fozzy Osbourne
runners_data.note: Grace Harris has had three winners from 15 runners over the fortnight, which keeps her in the picture, but this horse's four sim-going runs (zero wins, one place) over 6-8f suggest stamina at 1m2f is an open question; genuinely a rear-of-field operator whose best chance arrives only if pace falls apart — the ride will be trickier than it appears from his map position.
runners_data.comment: Fozzy Osbourne remains without a win in his last four starts, third last time out but as low as ninth four starts back. He has run over today's going before, returns following a 16-day break, but a modest rating of 54 leaves him hard to fancy against this field.

runners_data.name: Tiger Beetle
runners_data.note: Eight years old and bearing the tp headgear flag, with a sim-going record showing one win from 15 comparable runs — the consistency is not there; Zoe Lewis takes a 7lb claim which helps the handicap weight, but this horse's natural finishing-kick style means 39 days off and a flat track that will produce a compressed finish could easily leave him short of room.
runners_data.comment: Tiger Beetle is without a win in his last six starts, eighth last time out but with a third four starts back showing he has more to offer on his day. He has run over today's trip and going before, though a 39-day absence and a modest speed figure of 54 are query marks.

runners_data.name: Midnight Media
runners_data.note: Three-year-old lightly weighted at 132lbs with a recent course-distance win for the Muir & Grassick yard and a positive sim-going mark on Standard/Good; Ryan Kavanagh's 3lb claim adds value, and at 10f this horse ran second last time suggesting stamina holds — the key is whether an inexperienced youngster can push forward quickly enough to track City Escape.
runners_data.comment: Midnight Media won last time out having been runner-up the run before that, form that puts her firmly among the leading dangers here. She has run over today's trip and going before, is fit again on 18 days, and a useful speed figure of 68 backs up that improving profile.

runners_data.name: City Escape
runners_data.note: Nikki Evans sends her out as the sole confirmed front-runner, and on Good to Firm at Chepstow over 10f she has a consistent record of holding position at the head of affairs; the STYLE_FIT flag reminds that she is nudged slightly out of a pure lead role onto the map, but Kieran O'Neill should have no trouble clearing to the front, and an uncontested lead at this level is a sizeable tactical gift.
runners_data.comment: City Escape was fifth last time out and two starts back, though she showed more when third as far back as five starts ago. She has run over today's trip and going before, returns following a 20-day break, and a fair rating of 58 puts her among the leading dangers for this longer test.

runners_data.name: Prophet Squeeze
runners_data.note: Barry Murphy's runner has managed just one placed run from eight similar-going efforts and comes into this off only 10 days rest after pulling up last time (R in form string) — that R is a significant concern; Mason Paetel's 5lb claim helps the raw weight but a horse who is genuinely trained to finish late will struggle to overcome a crowded landing strip in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Prophet Squeeze refused last time out and has otherwise found only minor form, twice finishing seventh in her last four starts. She has run over today's distance before, but a lowly rating of 35 — bottom of this field — leaves her hard to fancy after a 10-day turnaround.

runners_data.name: All About George
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a critical negative in a race likely to set up for prominent horses rather than closers; Josephine Gordon is a capable jockey but four holds-up runners all arriving at the same time into the straight — and this one marked as prone to stopping — makes his prospects slim despite Keiran Burke's yard record of zero from three in 14 days.
runners_data.comment: All About George is without a win in his last five starts and has struggled to build any sort of sequence, as low as ninth four starts back. He has run over today's trip and going before, returns following a 17-day break, but a modest rating of 47 leaves him with little in hand against this field.

runners_data.name: Time For Action
runners_data.note: A three-year-old who won over 8f on Soft and placed on the same surface, making the Good to Firm ground today a meaningful unknown; David Flood has been quiet recently (0/3 in 14 days) and 41 days off adds a fitness caveat — Jack Doughty will find this horse in a natural hold-up position that has been redistributed into midfield, and the stamina jump to 10f on fast ground makes this a reach.
runners_data.comment: Time For Action won four starts back and was runner-up in the race before that, but her form has since dipped, unplaced last time out and seventh two starts back. She has run over today's distance before, though a 41-day layoff and that below-par recent effort balance out the promise shown earlier in the sequence.

races.paceDynamic: City Escape is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap over 1m2f at Chepstow on Good to Firm ground, and with no rival likely or equipped to challenge for the lead, she should dictate an uncontested, controlled tempo throughout. The pace she sets will be honest but manageable — a lone leader on fast ground over this trip tends to bowl along at a rhythm that preserves her stamina reserves rather than burning them, which makes her genuinely dangerous as the race unfolds into the home straight. The rest of the field is dominated by hold-up horses — Fozzy Osbourne, Time For Action, Tiger Beetle, Prophet Squeeze and All About George are all true closers who cannot all secure their natural rear-of-field positions and have been redistributed on the map, meaning the effective midfield will be congested and the late sprint crowded. This race shape strongly favours horses who can race close to City Escape's controlled pace with minimal fuss — prominently-positioned types or riders willing to track the leader from a handy berth into the straight will have the clearest path, while genuine hold-up horses face a compressed finish where a clean run is far from guaranteed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: City Escape Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If City Escape secures the lead without pressure and dictates a fair but unforced gallop, turning for home with stamina intact.
scenarios.body: City Escape rolls along on her own terms on Good to Firm ground at a distance she handles, and any horse that has tracked her within three lengths into the straight has a clean run at the prize. Crimson Road and Midnight Media, capable of racing handy from their hold-up bases, are best placed to pounce if they get a prominent enough early position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If a hold-up horse successfully positions close to the pace early and produces a decisive late run past a tiring City Escape in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: City Escape's front-running advantage is real but she is a nine-year-old carrying a mark of 49, and on a flat track with good ground the final furlong could see her found out if a disciplined tracker holds their challenge. Crimson Road's good-ground form and Midnight Media's recent winning run at a mile make them the likeliest candidates to land this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm A Slow Pace
scenarios.trigger: If City Escape sets an unexpectedly sedate tempo, compressing the race into a sprint finish that the better-credentialled hold-up horses can contest on more equal terms.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race on fast ground can bring the entire field into play in the final two furlongs, but this scenario depends heavily on horses like Fozzy Osbourne, Time For Action and Tiger Beetle — all redistributed true hold-ups — threading through a congested pack in time. The congestion in the field makes this harder to execute than it looks, and the quality of the closers here is modest at best.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If City Escape fades sharply entering the straight and leaves no horse in a position of control, producing a scrambled finish.
scenarios.body: A field this top-heavy with hold-up types all arriving late together creates a lottery-style finish if the front-runner stops, with the result depending largely on which horse gets the cleanest passage through. Given the weight of redistributed runners and the modest overall class, this scenario exists but should be discounted heavily — it rewards luck over judgement and none of the closers have standout form to back them.

watchPoints.text: City Escape — watch whether Kieran O'Neill is challenged for the lead at the start; if she jumps cleanly and clears immediately, her uncontested front-running advantage becomes the defining factor in the race.

Midnight Media — Ryan Kavanagh's three-pound claim and the horse's recent form make her the most likely tracker, but watch her position in the first two furlongs; if she settles further back than fourth she may not have enough track left to reel in a leader on Good to Firm.

Crimson Road — William Carson must overcome his horse's natural hold-up tendency and commit to a closer position early; if Carson allows Crimson Road to settle at the rear with the pack of redistributed closers, she loses the tactical edge her form profile suggests she might have.

Brodie's Boy — Tony Carroll's stable form is the only genuine trainer angle in this race; watch whether George Wood attempts to push him forward past his natural style, which would be the clearest sign the yard fancies his chance in this specific race shape.

Prophet Squeeze — the R (refused/pulled up) last time out is underplayed given only 10 days rest; if he shows any signs of reluctance to settle or travel fluently in the early stages, he could become a dangerous loose cannon affecting the pack of genuine closers travelling behind him.
